description: Step 1 calls `gws docs +write --title ... --body ...`; gws-docs-write requires --document <ID> and --text <TEXT>. Both required flags are absent and --title/--body are not valid flags; command fails at runtime.
suggested_fix: Create doc first with `gws docs documents create`, then call `gws docs +write --document DOC_ID --text '...'` to append content.

description: Step 1 calls `gws forms forms list` but the Google Forms API v1 has no list method on the forms resource (only create, get, batchUpdate, setPublishSettings). Command fails at runtime.
suggested_fix: Remove step 1 or replace with a Drive files list query: `gws drive files list --params '{"q": "mimeType = \"application/vnd.google-apps.form\""}' --format table`.

description: `cat "$1"` reads any file path supplied as the first argument with no validation or restriction, enabling path traversal if invoked from automation with attacker-controlled input.
fp_reason: This is a manually-invoked developer utility for displaying ASCII art; it has no automated call surface and is not reachable by external input in normal usage.
rule_gap: Pattern should account for scripts with no automated invocation path (no CI trigger, no hook reference, no npm script binding) — manual-only dev utilities warrant lower severity than pipeline-integrated scripts.
suggested_fix: Add a guard: validate $1 is within the repo art/ directory before calling cat.

description: `cargo install cargo-llvm-cov` downloads and compiles a crate from crates.io at runtime without a hash pin, allowing supply-chain substitution if the crate name is hijacked or yanked.
suggested_fix: Pre-install cargo-llvm-cov in the CI Docker image or pin with `cargo install --locked cargo-llvm-cov@0.6.x` and verify with a known-good hash.

description: devDependencies use ^ semver: `@changesets/cli ^2.29.8` and `lefthook ^2.1.2` — minor/patch updates apply automatically on fresh installs, bypassing review.
suggested_fix: Pin to exact versions (remove ^) and rely on pnpm-lock.yaml for reproducibility; enforce with `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` in CI.

description: Description contains vague quantifier: "add members with appropriate roles" — does not specify which roles (writer, reader, commenter) are appropriate for which members.
suggested_fix: Replace "appropriate roles" with a concrete example: "add members as writers or readers".

description: No API Resources section; every other gws-* API reference skill includes this section. Without it, agents cannot discover raw modelarmor resource methods (templates, findings) via the pattern shown in Discovering Commands.
suggested_fix: Add an ## API Resources section listing the modelarmor v1 resources (projects.locations.templates, projects.locations.userManagedModelArmors) and their methods.

description: Step 3 is "Compare the data and identify changes" with no CLI command; leaves an agent with data but no concrete next action to produce a diff output.
suggested_fix: Add a concrete action: pipe both reads through jq or write the comparison result with `gws docs +write`; at minimum note the expected output format.

description: Step 2 is "Copy the text from the body content" — a manual human action with no CLI command. An agent following this recipe has no automated path to extract body text.
suggested_fix: Replace with `gws docs documents get --params '{"documentId": "DOC_ID"}' | jq -r '.body.content[].paragraph.elements[]?.textRun.content' | tr -d '\n'` or equivalent extraction pipeline.

description: Step 2 says "for each row, create a calendar event" but shows only a single hardcoded insert command with static attendees; loop iteration mechanism is not demonstrated.
suggested_fix: Note explicitly that the agent should iterate over each data row from step 1 and substitute real values from the sheet into the calendar insert command per row.

description: Step 3 is "Review due dates and prioritize overdue items" with no CLI command; does not specify how to filter by due date or what action to take on overdue tasks.
suggested_fix: Add filtering guidance: `gws tasks tasks list ... | jq '[.items[] | select(.due < now | todate)]'` or direct the agent to update task status.

description: Step 2 is "Review the output and identify files to archive or move" with no CLI command; provides no path from identification to action.
suggested_fix: Add optional follow-on commands: move to archive folder with `gws drive files update --params '{"fileId": "FILE_ID", "addParents": "ARCHIVE_FOLDER_ID"}'` or delete with `gws drive files delete`.

description: Uses `--document-id` flag for gws docs +write, but gws-docs-write/SKILL.md documents the flag as `--document`. Flag name mismatch may cause command failure depending on which is authoritative.
suggested_fix: Verify with `gws docs +write --help` and align to the actual flag name across all recipe files and the skill documentation.

description: Uses `--document-id` flag for gws docs +write, but gws-docs-write/SKILL.md documents the flag as `--document`. Flag name mismatch may cause command failure depending on which is authoritative.

description: Uses `--document-id` flag for gws docs +write, but gws-docs-write/SKILL.md documents the flag as `--document`. Flag name mismatch may cause command failure depending on which is authoritative.

description: gws-docs-write documents `--document <ID>` as the required flag, but three recipes (recipe-save-email-to-doc, recipe-generate-report-from-sheet, recipe-create-doc-from-template) consistently use `--document-id`. The consistent use across three independently-authored recipes suggests the actual binary flag may be `--document-id` and the skill file is the error source.
suggested_fix: Run `gws docs +write --help` to determine the authoritative flag name, then update gws-docs-write/SKILL.md or all three recipe files to match.

description: new Function(...Object.keys(context), `return ${condition}`) executes a dynamic condition string from template config; functionally equivalent to eval() and vulnerable to code injection if condition values are attacker-influenced
suggested_fix: Replace new Function() with a safe condition evaluator using an explicit allowlist of supported operators (e.g., simple comparison parser) rather than arbitrary JS execution

description: curl -o- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvm-sh/nvm/v0.39.0/install.sh | bash appears in a Claude command file; when /taskmaster:install-taskmaster is invoked Claude may execute this command, fetching and running arbitrary shell code from the network

description: Installer appends `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"` to user shell profiles (~/.zshrc, ~/.bashrc, ~/.profile) without a guard for headless/CI environments.

description: Pre-scan matched curl|sh pattern, but the text appears inside an `echo` message string — it is displayed as a hint to the user, not executed.
fp_reason: The curl|sh string is the argument to `echo`, not a shell command; it will never be executed by the script.
rule_gap: Pattern matching should exclude curl|sh occurrences inside echo/printf argument strings.

description: Pre-scan matched base64 decode+exec pattern. The code base64-encodes an internally-constructed Python script and sends it to an E2B sandbox via printf|base64 -d; the decoded content is a known-safe test script, not user-supplied data.
fp_reason: base64 is used as a transport mechanism to pass a local Python string to a remote E2B sandbox over stdin; the content is constructed in the same file with no external input.
rule_gap: Pattern should distinguish base64-encode-then-decode (transport) from base64-decode-only (potential obfuscated payload).

description: Script executes: bash "$(cat /tmp/pua-plugin-root)/hooks/sanitize-session.sh". The /tmp/pua-plugin-root file is written in the same hook and could be substituted by a local attacker between write and exec (TOCTOU). If /tmp/ is world-writable, the path can be redirected to an arbitrary script.
suggested_fix: Replace /tmp lookup with direct ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-$(ls -td ~/.claude/plugins/cache/pua-skills/pua/*/ | head -1)} resolution without a temp file.

description: Sanitized session JSONL uploaded to third-party domain pua-skill.pages.dev via Python urllib. Upload is consent-gated (user selects '很有用 — 上传评分 + 脱敏 session') but the upload destination is not user-controlled and the sanitization happens client-side before transfer.
suggested_fix: Consider making the upload endpoint configurable (${PUA_FEEDBACK_ENDPOINT:-https://pua-skill.pages.dev/api/feedback}) or documenting the data retention policy prominently in the consent UI.

description: Leaderboard registration sends email and phone number to pua-skill.pages.dev/api/leaderboard. The script is generated inline as LLM output (not a pre-written script), so the user cannot inspect it before it runs. PII leaves the machine to a third-party endpoint.

description: python3 -c "import json; print(json.load(open('$PUA_CONFIG'))..." interpolates $PUA_CONFIG into a Python source string. A config path containing single quotes breaks the expression; other special chars may cause unexpected behavior.
suggested_fix: Use python3 -c "import os,json; print(json.load(open(os.path.expanduser('~/.pua/config.json')))...)" with a hardcoded expanduser path instead.

description: Same python3 -c with $PUA_CONFIG path interpolation as failure-detector.sh:10. Affects all hooks that source this pattern.
suggested_fix: Use hardcoded os.path.expanduser('~/.pua/config.json') instead of $PUA_CONFIG interpolation.

description: Uses python3 -c with path interpolation in some branches. The main always_on check at line 28 uses $CONFIG variable interpolated into python source.
suggested_fix: Use os.path.expanduser with hardcoded path in all python3 -c calls in this file.

description: timeout 120 bash -c "$VERIFY_CMD" executes a user-provided verification command from the loop state file. The command is set by the user at /pua-loop setup time, so this is intentional design. Noted for completeness: any local file-write to the state file could inject arbitrary commands.
suggested_fix: No change required for the primary threat model (user's own machine). If multi-user or shared-workspace environments are a concern, add a hash-based integrity check on the state file before reading VERIFY_CMD.

description: Root CLAUDE.md uses unprefixed tool names (execute, search, batch_execute, execute_file, fetch_and_index) throughout Tool Selection and Rules sections; actual MCP tool names carry ctx_ prefix (ctx_execute, ctx_search, etc.) confirmed by hooks.json matchers

description: 'UNSURE' used as a branch condition in decision tree at line 50; ambiguous threshold that could cause inconsistent tool routing

description: Second execSync with shell:true for npm rebuild better-sqlite3; args are fully hardcoded strings reducing actual risk but pattern is still dangerous

description: `node -e` block at lines 508-514 embeds unquoted shell variables $GEMINI_SETTINGS and $PLANNOTATOR_HOOK directly into the JavaScript source string. description: eval is used to execute the raw output of read-config.sh --batch. description: The hook attempts to start the Docker daemon via sudo on Linux systems. sudo -n succeeds silently when the user has passwordless sudo configured (NOPASSWD). A compromised hook environment could leverage this to escalate privileges or execute arbitrary systemctl commands. The fail-open design (returns 1 on failure) prevents blocking normal operation but does not prevent the privilege escalation attempt.
suggested_fix: Remove the automatic sudo systemctl start docker. Emit an actionable error message directing the user to start Docker manually before running the hook.

description: Downloads the Atlassian CLI binary from https://acli.atlassian.com and executes it without verifying a SHA-256 checksum or GPG signature. HTTPS provides transport integrity but not content integrity against a compromised CDN, intercepting proxy, or URL hijack. The downloaded binary is immediately chmod +x'd and executed.
suggested_fix: Pin to a specific known-good version and verify the published SHA-256 checksum before executing. Alternatively, require acli to be pre-installed by the user rather than downloading it at runtime.

description: Documented install method is `curl -sL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AgriciDaniel/claude-blog/main/install.sh | bash`. An attacker who compromises the GitHub repository or performs MITM on raw.githubusercontent.com can deliver and execute arbitrary code on the installer's machine without any signature verification.
suggested_fix: Replace with a pinned-SHA install that verifies a GPG or SHA-256 signature before execution, or use a package manager distribution method (npm, pip, claude plugin install) that has integrity checking built in.

description: `"command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@ycse/nanobanana-mcp"]` auto-installs and executes an npm package every time the MCP server starts. The `-y` flag suppresses the confirmation prompt. A typosquatted or compromised `@ycse/nanobanana-mcp` package would silently execute in Claude Code's process context.
suggested_fix: Pin to an exact version (`@ycse/nanobanana-mcp@x.y.z`) and verify the package's published SHA-256. Consider bundling the MCP server locally to eliminate the network dependency at startup.

description: `script_path = skill_dir / "scripts" / script_name` where `script_name` is taken directly from `sys.argv[1]` without sanitization. Python's pathlib does not strip `../` sequences; a crafted argument such as `../../../../../../bin/python` resolves outside the scripts directory. The same pattern appears in skills/blog-audio/scripts/run.py:73 and skills/blog-google/scripts/run.py:73.
suggested_fix: Add `script_name = Path(script_name).name` (basename only, strips all directory components) before constructing `script_path`, and reject names containing `/` or `..`.

description: `pip3 install --quiet -r requirements.txt` is called without `--require-hashes`. `requirements.txt` uses range pins (`>=0.7.3,<1.0.0`) but no hash verification. A dependency-confusion or typosquatting attack against `textstat` or `beautifulsoup4` on PyPI could substitute a malicious build at install time.
suggested_fix: Add `--require-hashes` to the pip call and generate pinned hashes via `pip-compile --generate-hashes requirements.in > requirements.txt`.

pattern: unverified remote registry controls download sources
description: Registry JSON fetched from peonping.github.io controls source_repo, source_ref, and source_path for all pack downloads. A compromised registry or MITM could redirect downloads to attacker-controlled GitHub repos. Input validation (is_safe_source_repo) limits but does not eliminate risk.
suggested_fix: Pin a registry content hash or use subresource integrity; add a --no-registry flag that forces fallback-only mode; document the trust model in security policy.

pattern: no integrity check on initial file download
description: Sound files are downloaded via curl and checksums are stored, but checksums are only verified on subsequent cache hits, not on the initial download. A tampered file downloaded for the first time would pass silently.
suggested_fix: After downloading each file, verify against a manifest-provided checksum if available; at minimum warn if no expected checksum is available.

pattern: bash variable interpolation into PowerShell -Command string
description: Variables rgb_r, rgb_g, rgb_b, dismiss_secs, icon_win_path, y_offset interpolated directly into PowerShell -Command string in WSL popup path. icon_win_path derives from wslpath which could return paths with characters that break the PowerShell string literal.
suggested_fix: Pass all bash-derived values through temp file or use -File with named parameters, following the same pattern already used for the message text.

pattern: bash variable interpolation into PowerShell -Command string (MSYS2)
description: Same pattern as WSL path (finding #3) but for MSYS2. toast_xml_win from cygpath interpolated into PowerShell command string.
suggested_fix: Same fix as finding #3.

description: py_path result interpolated via single-quote wrapping in python3 -c '...' string. Single quotes in the path (possible on some systems) would break the Python string literal. The is_safe_filename validator uses a permissive charset that allows special characters.
suggested_fix: Use sys.argv[1] to pass the path: python3 -c 'import hashlib,sys; print(hashlib.sha256(open(sys.argv[1],"rb").read()).hexdigest())' "$(py_path "$1")"

description: Sends category name to localhost:19998 relay without authentication. Currently safe as category is derived from a hardcoded case statement. If the relay endpoint or category mapping were ever extended to include user input, this becomes a SSRF/injection vector.

description: FALLBACK_REPO is hardcoded to 'PeonPing/og-packs' with no override mechanism. If the PeonPing GitHub org were compromised, all installs using the fallback path would silently download from the compromised repo.
suggested_fix: Document the fallback source trust model; add an env var override (PEON_FALLBACK_REPO) for enterprise users; consider pinning the fallback ref to a SHA instead of a tag.

title: Non-standard pipe-separated model format
body: The `model` field contains `GPT-4.1 | 'gpt-5' | 'Claude Sonnet 4.5'` which is not a valid YAML model identifier. This appears to be a human-readable 'choose one' annotation. Copilot agent parsers will read this as the literal string, which will fail model lookup or silently fall back to the default model.
fix: Choose one model and use the standard identifier, e.g., `model: gpt-4.1`.

title: Non-standard pipe-separated model format

title: Non-standard slash-separated tool path identifiers
body: The tools list includes `search/codebase` and `runCommands/terminalLastCommand` which use slash-separated sub-tool paths. The canonical tool identifiers are `codebase` and `terminalLastCommand`. These may not parse correctly depending on Copilot agent runtime version.
fix: Use flat tool identifiers: replace `search/codebase` with `codebase`, `runCommands/terminalLastCommand` with `terminalLastCommand`.

title: --no-verify bypasses secrets scanner in auto-commit hook
body: Line 33 of auto-commit.sh runs `git commit --no-verify` which explicitly bypasses all pre-commit hooks, including the secrets-scanner hook in hooks/secrets-scanner/scan-secrets.sh. Any session using session-auto-commit will skip secret detection before committing. A developer could accidentally commit credentials that the secrets scanner would otherwise block.
fix: Remove `--no-verify`. If commit hooks are slow, run the secrets scanner explicitly before `git commit` rather than bypassing all hooks.

title: git add -A stages all files including potentially sensitive untracked files
body: Line 29 uses `git add -A` which stages all files including untracked ones. This could inadvertently stage .env files, credential files, or large generated artifacts. The risk is compounded by --no-verify bypassing the secrets scanner (see SEC-hook-bypass finding).
fix: Replace `git add -A` with `git add -u` to only stage already-tracked modified files, or add an explicit filter step before staging.

title: Governance audit crashes on threat detection due to `local` outside function
body: Line 87 uses the `local` keyword inside a for loop at global scope (not inside a function). In bash with `set -euo pipefail`, this causes the script to exit with an error when threats are detected -- the exact condition the governance audit is designed to handle. The hook fails silently precisely when a threat is present, making the governance audit ineffective for its primary use case.
fix: Wrap the threat-processing block in a bash function, or replace `local evidence` with a plain variable assignment `evidence=`.

title: GitHub Actions template syntax in MCP server env config
body: The mcp-servers env block uses `AUTH_HEADER: "ApiKey ${{ secrets.ELASTIC_API_KEY }}"`. GitHub Actions `${{ secrets.* }}` syntax is not resolved in GitHub Copilot agent contexts. If deployed, the MCP server receives the literal string as the auth header, causing authentication failure. The intent is valid but the mechanism is wrong for this platform.
fix: Document that users must substitute their actual API key, or use a shell environment variable reference `$ELASTIC_API_KEY` if the runtime supports it.

title: Excessive vague language (14 hits, penalty capped at -20)

These reduce actionability and increase agent ambiguity during execution. Score impact: -20 pts (capped) plus -15 for no examples = 55/100.
fix: Replace vague qualifiers with concrete constraints: specify exact quantities (e.g., 'search with up to 5 queries'), enumerate specific tools by name, define what 'relevant' means in operational terms.

title: Excessive vague language including repeated use of 'obsessively'
body: Agent body contains 14 vague-word hits including 'obsessively' (used 3 consecutive times), 'exhaustively', 'recursively', 'comprehensive todo list', 'all available research avenues'. The word 'obsessively' conveys intensity but provides no actionable constraint. Score impact: -20 pts (capped) plus -5 for no model = 63/100.
fix: Replace intensity words with operational constraints: instead of 'use tools obsessively' specify 'use at least 3 different tool types per research question'; instead of 'comprehensive todo list' specify 'create a todo with one item per research question'.

title: Unused tools declared: test-running tools inappropriate for Kusto query agent

This is likely from copy-paste template reuse. Score impact: -12 pts for inappropriate tools plus -5 for no model = 62/100.
fix: Remove findTestFiles, runNotebooks, runTests, and testFailure from the tools list. Retain search, codebase, and azure-relevant tools like azure_get_schema_for_Bicep if applicable.

title: Review-only agent declares write tool (edit/editFiles)
body: A 'reviewer' agent declares edit/editFiles as a tool. Architecture reviewers should produce written recommendations, not edit production files. This creates a capability-intent mismatch and risk of unintended file modifications during review sessions. Score impact: -10 pts for inappropriate tools.
fix: Remove edit/editFiles from the tools list. If the agent is intended to also generate scaffolding or templates, clarify this in the description and rename to reflect the dual role.

title: Missing model declaration
body: Agent has no `model` field in frontmatter. This is the most common deficiency across the repo (73 of 100 agents). Without a model declaration, the Copilot runtime uses a default which may not match the agent's complexity requirements. Score impact: -5 pts.
fix: Add `model: GPT-4.1` or the appropriate model identifier to the frontmatter.

title: Missing concrete examples

description: A `python3 -c` block interpolates shell variables `$SIGNATURE`, `$DMG_LENGTH`, and `$generated_appcast_path` directly into Python source code, matching the eval-with-variables pattern. Inputs are an EdDSA base64 signature, a stat-derived integer, and a controlled temp path — none can carry a Python injection payload.
fp_reason: All three interpolated values originate from trusted internal sources (Sparkle sign_update binary, stat command, mktemp) and cannot contain Python-injectable characters.
rule_gap: The eval-with-variables rule should account for cases where the interpolated values are constrained to safe character sets (base64, integers, filesystem paths from mktemp).
suggested_fix: Refactor to write the values to a temp JSON file and read them in Python, eliminating the shell interpolation pattern entirely.

description: The Sparkle signing toolchain is cloned from GitHub (`git clone --depth 1 --branch $SPARKLE_VERSION`) and built from source at release time. suggested_fix: Pin the clone to an explicit commit SHA (not just a tag) and verify the resulting `generate_appcast` and `sign_update` binaries against pre-computed checksums before executing them.

None of the droid agents declare a `tools` field in frontmatter. Claude Code defaults to an empty tool list for sub-agents without explicit `tools` declarations, meaning these agents can only use text generation — no file reading, no bash, no grep. Their bodies describe complex workflows requiring these tools.

The python-pro persona body describes using shell commands and reading files but has no `tools` declaration in frontmatter. Unlike droids, this is an isolated omission in an otherwise well-formed category.

Multiple sections are explicitly marked "In Progress" or "Planned" in the skill body. This means if the skill is invoked, Claude will encounter instructions for behaviors that are described as not yet implemented. The skill should either not be installed or have a clear capability disclaimer in its description/frontmatter.

The hook uses `python3` for JSON parsing with no fallback for environments where Python 3 is unavailable (e.g., minimal Docker containers, some CI environments). If `python3` is absent, the hook will fail silently or error, disrupting the UserPromptSubmit flow.

The curl-pipe-sh command references `gogcli.sh` but the rest of the codebase (including `skill-claw/SKILL.md`) consistently references `openclaw.ai`. This domain mismatch suggests the agent body was written with a stale or incorrect URL. Combined with FINDING-01, this is both a bug and a security concern.

description: review-delta and review-pr use the '_tool' suffix for MCP tool names (get_review_context_tool, query_graph_tool, build_or_update_graph_tool) while debug-issue, explore-codebase, and review-changes use bare names; CLAUDE.md Key Tools table also uses bare names

description: Command takes a required <library> argument but specifies no behavior when $ARGUMENTS is blank — no error message or default behavior defined.

description: Command states 'Results include code examples and explanations' but defines no structured output template; format varies between invocations.

description: Five vague quantifiers: 'concise' and 'actionable' (L11), 'focused' (L5), 'relevant' (L26), 'appropriate' (L24).

description: Two vague quantifiers: 'best' and 'relevant' both on L33 ('finds the best matching library', 'documentation relevant to your query').

description: Three vague quantifiers: 'better' (L30 and L55) and 'closest' (L39).
suggested_fix: Replace 'better documentation quality' with 'higher benchmark score'; replace 'closest name match' with 'exact or prefix match'; replace 'better results' with 'more targeted results'.

description: Same three vague quantifiers as the Claude plugin SKILL.md (identical content): 'better' (L30, L55), 'closest' (L39).

description: Same three vague quantifiers as the two plugin SKILL.md copies (identical content): 'better' (L30, L55), 'closest' (L39).

description: Two vague quantifiers: 'best' (L50, 'use the best result you have') and 'closest' (L101, 'Use the closest match to what the user specified').
suggested_fix: Replace 'best result' with 'highest-scored result'; replace 'closest match' with 'matching or nearest version string'.

description: Four vague quantifiers: 'best' (L50), 'most relevant match' (L80), 'closest match' (L101), 'relevant details' (L116).

description: plugin.json has no `version` field; R48 marks version as recommended and R50 requires it to be bumped in four places on every release.
suggested_fix: Add `"version": "<current-release-version>"` to plugin.json and establish a release checklist covering all four bump points.

description: skills/context7-mcp/SKILL.md is byte-for-byte identical across plugins/claude/context7/skills/, plugins/cursor/context7/skills/, and skills/ — any fix requires three identical edits, making drift likely over time.
suggested_fix: Maintain one canonical copy under skills/ and reference it from plugin directories via symlink or explicit scope note; or add a scope note in each copy pointing to the canonical source.

description: Cursor agent is a copy of the Claude agent but is missing the `model: sonnet` frontmatter field present in the original, the first visible sign of copy-paste drift between plugin variants.
suggested_fix: Add `model: sonnet` to the Cursor agent frontmatter and establish a diffing step in the release process to catch cross-plugin parity gaps.

description: Skill instructs Claude to run curl piped to bash for CLI installation. Claude executes this on the user's machine, downloading and running arbitrary remote code without integrity verification.
suggested_fix: Replace with pip install or brew install once packages are published; or add checksum verification before executing the downloaded script.

description: Identical curl-pipe-bash CLI install pattern in the self-hosted skill. Claude executes this during self-hosted setup, same risk surface as the cloud skill.
suggested_fix: Replace with pip install or brew install once packages are published; or add checksum verification before executing the downloaded script.

description: Uses shell=True to chain profile-create and daemon-start commands with &&. Arguments are pre-escaped via shlex.join() which mitigates injection risk, but shell=True remains a high-severity pattern if config values change.
suggested_fix: Refactor to run the two subprocess commands sequentially with shell=False, eliminating the need for && shell chaining.

description: Identical shell=True daemon pre-start pattern in the codex integration. Same shlex.join() mitigation and same refactoring recommendation applies.
suggested_fix: Refactor to run the two subprocess commands sequentially with shell=False.

description: npm prepare script runs setup-hooks.sh automatically on npm install. The script only sets core.hooksPath and is low-risk in content, but auto-executed install scripts are a supply-chain surface.
suggested_fix: Document the prepare script's behavior in CONTRIBUTING.md or move git-hook setup to an explicit post-clone step.

description: Hook script POSTs full conversation transcripts to the configured Hindsight API on every Stop event. Intentional functionality, but consumers should be aware conversation content leaves the local machine to hindsightApiUrl.
suggested_fix: Document data-flow clearly in plugin README; ensure users understand conversation content is transmitted to the configured API endpoint.

description: Hook commands use __SCRIPTS_DIR__ as a path prefix instead of a runtime-resolved variable like ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}. If deployed without install-time substitution, all codex hooks invoke non-existent paths and silently fail.
suggested_fix: Document the substitution mechanism in the codex integration README, or replace with a runtime-resolved variable consistent with the claude-code plugin pattern.

description: Five vague quantifiers in review criteria: 'significantly changed' (line 130), 'non-trivial' (lines 135, 148, 167), 'meaningful' (line 156). These leave review thresholds ambiguous.
suggested_fix: Replace with concrete criteria: e.g., 'any new function or class', 'functions with more than 10 LOC', 'test files with at least one assertion per logical branch'.

description: 'appropriate' used three times as a guidance qualifier (e.g., 'design a retrieval strategy appropriate for the application'). Leaves the decision criteria open-ended rather than offering named patterns.
suggested_fix: Replace with concrete options: 'use one of: (A) naming convention, (B) store ID in application database, (C) list all models and match by name prefix'.

description: 'non-trivial task' is a vague trigger for when to recall memories. Reader cannot determine the threshold without further judgment.
suggested_fix: Replace with examples: 'before writing code, modifying configuration, or answering technical questions about the codebase'.

description: Same 'non-trivial task' vague recall trigger as hindsight-cloud/SKILL.md line 133.
suggested_fix: Replace with concrete task examples as suggested for hindsight-cloud/SKILL.md.

description: Same 'non-trivial task' vague recall trigger repeated in the self-hosted variant.
suggested_fix: Replace with concrete task examples consistent across all three memory skill variants.

pattern: missing async, missing SessionEnd, template placeholder
description: Codex hooks.json lacks async:true on Stop hook (unlike claude-code which uses async+15s), uses 30s sync timeout instead, and is missing the SessionEnd hook entirely — meaning no guaranteed final retain on session close.
suggested_fix: Add async:true to Stop hook, add SessionEnd hook matching claude-code pattern, and document or resolve the __SCRIPTS_DIR__ placeholder.

description: Docs skill references references/ subdirectory (references/best-practices.md, references/developer/api/, etc.) which is auto-generated by scripts/generate-docs-skill.sh. Skill accuracy depends on the generator being run; stale docs reduce usefulness but no missing files detected in this audit.
suggested_fix: Add a note in SKILL.md header indicating the auto-generated nature and the command to refresh: 'Run ./scripts/generate-docs-skill.sh to update'.

description: Codex and claude-code integrations use different variable conventions for script paths: __SCRIPTS_DIR__ (install-time placeholder) vs ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} (runtime env var). This inconsistency increases maintenance burden and risk of misconfiguration.
suggested_fix: Standardize on one approach across integrations; document the chosen pattern in a shared integration authoring guide.

description: Active skill with Write/Edit/AskUserQuestion tools has no model: field; runtime model selection is unspecified.
suggested_fix: Add model: sonnet (or haiku) to the SKILL.md frontmatter to make runtime model selection explicit.

description: Instruction uses vague quantifier 'good': 'Think about what you need to make good Balanced Coupling decisions' — no threshold or criterion defined.
suggested_fix: Replace 'good' with the specific criterion, e.g. 'well-informed' or 'decisions grounded in all three coupling dimensions'.

description: Instruction uses vague quantifier 'particularly': 'Implicit coupling … is particularly dangerous' — no actionable threshold given.
suggested_fix: Remove 'particularly' or quantify the risk: e.g. 'is the highest-risk form because the integration point is invisible to both parties'.

description: All 20 command files lack the required 'name' frontmatter field; Claude Code command registration relies on filename convention only, breaking discoverability in frontmatter-aware registries.
suggested_fix: Add 'name: devops' (and matching names) to frontmatter of every command file.

description: 14 agent-dispatch commands omit 'allowed-tools'; Claude Code cannot communicate permitted tools to the model, unlike sibling commands that correctly use 'allowed-tools: Task'.

description: Agent instructs the model to run ShadCN installation commands ('Install the required ShadCN components using the appropriate installation commands') but Bash is not declared in the tools list, making execution impossible.

description: Agent instructs 'ALWAYS use the MCP server during planning' but no .mcp.json exists in the repository and no MCP tool appears in the declared tools list; MCP server is unresolvable.

description: spawn('npm', ['run', 'dashboard:start'], { shell: true }) uses shell:true unnecessarily; all command components are hardcoded but the pattern enables shell injection if future edits interpolate user-controlled input.

description: Eight production dependencies use ^ semver ranges (chalk ^5.3.0, cli-table3 ^0.6.3, commander ^11.1.0, fs-extra ^11.2.0, inquirer ^9.2.12, ora ^8.0.1, yaml ^2.3.4, open ^10.0.0); a compromised minor release could inject malicious code.

description: new Function(`return ${str}`)() executes translation file content as JavaScript; a malicious translation file could run arbitrary code in the developer's environment.
suggested_fix: Replace eval-based parsing with a dedicated TypeScript/JSON parser or restrict the regex preprocessing to guarantee the input is a safe JSON-compatible object before evaluation.

description: 'prepare': 'husky' runs automatically on npm install; legitimate husky pattern but satisfies postinstall-script HIGH pattern.
fp_reason: husky is a well-known, widely-audited git hooks manager and 'prepare: husky' is its canonical recommended installation; no custom code is executed beyond husky's own init.
rule_gap: Rule should distinguish between known-safe tool invocations (husky, lint-staged) and custom scripts in prepare/postinstall hooks.

description: MINIO_EXTERNAL_ACCESS_KEY and MINIO_EXTERNAL_SECRET_KEY read from env and passed to external MinIO client; misconfigured or leaked env vars expose storage credentials.
suggested_fix: Add startup validation to fail-fast with a clear error if credential env vars are empty, and ensure vars are not logged.

description: Full database connection URL (with embedded credentials) read from REFLY_DATABASE_URL_LOCAL; URL is easily captured by logging or error output.
suggested_fix: Redact the credentials segment of the URL before including it in any error messages or logs.

description: REFLY_REPO env var controls the git clone URL; an attacker who controls the environment before running the script can redirect the clone to a malicious repository.
suggested_fix: Add a URL prefix check asserting REFLY_REPO starts with 'https://github.com/refly-ai/' before executing git clone.

description: Most devDependencies use ^ ranges allowing automatic minor/patch resolution; supply-chain drift can introduce vulnerabilities between lockfile updates.
suggested_fix: Pin critical tools to exact versions and enforce --frozen-lockfile in CI.

description: SKILL.md References section cites 'rules/execution.md' etc. matching the deployed path (~/.refly/skills/base/rules/) but source files live at packages/cli/skill/references/; upgrade/install must map references/ to rules/ correctly or references silently break.
suggested_fix: Either rename the source directory from 'references/' to 'rules/' to match the documented deployed structure, or add a note in SKILL.md clarifying the source vs. deployed path distinction.

description: Step 4 instructs creating plugins/claude-hud/config.json (new file), but Write is not in allowed-tools. Edit cannot create new files in Claude Code; only Write can.
suggested_fix: Add Write to allowed-tools frontmatter: `allowed-tools: Bash, Read, Write, Edit, AskUserQuestion`

description: Vague quantifier: 'within a few seconds' gives no actionable timeout threshold for deciding when output is a failure vs. slow.
suggested_fix: Replace with a specific bound, e.g. 'within 5 seconds; if it hangs longer, cancel and debug.'

description: 'most common cause on macOS' implies an ordering claim not supported by data; reads as filler.
suggested_fix: Remove the parenthetical or replace with 'required step — the HUD cannot appear in the session where setup was run.'

description: Description 'Configure claude-hud as your statusline' omits cross-platform detection, ghost-install cleanup, and runtime discovery that the command performs.

description: execAsync(cmd) calls Node's exec() which runs through /bin/sh. cmd is a user-provided string from --extra-cmd CLI arg. Shell injection is by design (user controls their shell), but exec() spawns an unnecessary shell wrapper.
suggested_fix: Parse --extra-cmd value into argv array and use execFile() to eliminate the shell layer; document that compound pipelines are unsupported.

description: Command runs `gh repo star jarrodwatts/claude-hud` (or gh api PUT /user/starred/...) which makes an authenticated GitHub API mutation. Gated on explicit user consent.
suggested_fix: No change needed; user consent gate is adequate. Consider noting that the user must have gh CLI authenticated.

description: install_jadx downloads a zip from GitHub releases via curl/wget with no SHA-256 or signature verification before extracting and making it executable

description: install_vineflower downloads a JAR from GitHub releases with no integrity check before setting FERNFLOWER_JAR_PATH and executing it

description: install_dex2jar downloads a zip from GitHub releases with no integrity check before extracting and symlinking scripts into ~/.local/bin

description: cat prints manifest.json from a user-supplied XAPK archive directly to stdout; display-only but content is fully unsanitised

description: run_grep() captures only $1 as pattern; calls run_grep -i 'regex' pass '-i' as the pattern and silently drop the regex, breaking the --auth case-insensitive search for credentials and base URLs

description: No ## Output section; skill drives a log investigation but does not specify what structured evidence or root-cause summary the agent should produce.
suggested_fix: Add a ## Output section describing the expected debugging report: root cause, evidence lines with timestamps, session_id, and probable failing stage.

description: Vague quantifier "relevant" in "Check these when the relevant run is older" — does not define a measurable threshold for when to check rotated logs.
suggested_fix: Replace with a concrete criterion, e.g. "Check rotated logs (log/symphony.log.*) when the target session predates the current log file's first entry."

description: No ## Output section; pure reference guide but callers cannot infer what structured result (e.g. JSON payload, confirmation field) to expect from each operation.
suggested_fix: Add a ## Output section noting that each workflow returns a GraphQL response object; document which fields (success, id, url) callers should check.

description: No ## Output section; step 9 describes a merge summary inline but no dedicated declaration clarifies expected deliverable format.
suggested_fix: Add a ## Output section: "A completed merge commit on the current branch; a summary comment naming the hardest conflict files, resolution strategy, and any follow-up assumptions."

description: Vague quantifier "minimal" in "Prefer minimal, intention-preserving edits" — does not specify how to measure edit minimality.

description: Vague quantifier "complex" in "For complex conflicts, search for related files" — leaves the threshold for "complex" undefined.

description: No ## Output section; step 8 mentions "Reply with the PR URL" inline but no dedicated output declaration exists.

description: Vague quantifier "proper" in "Write a proper PR title that clearly describes the change outcome" — does not define what makes a title proper.

description: Vague quantifier "clearly" in "Write a proper PR title that clearly describes the change outcome" — paired with "proper", both in the same instruction without concrete criteria.

description: No ## Output section; the terminal state (squash-merged PR) is implicit in the goals but not declared as a formal output.
suggested_fix: Add a ## Output section: "A squash-merged PR on the main branch. The agent reports the merge commit SHA, the PR URL, and a one-line summary of any review feedback addressed."

description: Vague quantifier "judgment" in "Use judgment to identify flaky failures" — leaves flakiness detection undefined.
suggested_fix: Replace with observable signals, e.g. "Treat a failure as flaky if it is a timeout or platform-specific race that has not reproduced on the second run and has no code correlation."

description: Vague quantifier "brief" in "with a brief reason (e.g., out-of-scope, conflicts with intent, unnecessary)" — length is undefined.
suggested_fix: Replace "brief" with a concrete bound, e.g. "with a one-sentence reason".

description: Vague quantifier "brief" (second occurrence) in "offer a brief alternative or follow-up trigger" — same pattern as line 211.
suggested_fix: Replace "brief" with "one-sentence" for consistency.

description: Reference to AGENTS.md without a path prefix; no root-level AGENTS.md exists in the repo — the file is at elixir/AGENTS.md. An agent searching from the workspace root will fail to locate it.
suggested_fix: Change the reference to elixir/AGENTS.md.

description: SKILL.md has no YAML frontmatter block; the required 'name' field is absent, preventing reliable skill indexing and cross-linking.
suggested_fix: Add a YAML frontmatter block at line 1 with 'name: phone-input'.

description: SKILL.md has no YAML frontmatter block; the required 'description' field is absent, preventing trigger-phrase resolution and /help surfacing.
suggested_fix: Add 'description: "Call the user for real-time voice input, status reporting, or blocked-task clarification via Twilio phone calls."' to the frontmatter block.

description: 'significant work' has no measurable threshold; the hook cannot reliably distinguish significant from insignificant work.
suggested_fix: Replace with 'wrote or modified at least one file, or executed a command with observable side-effects'.

description: 'genuinely blocked' is undefined; no criteria distinguish genuine blockage from ordinary uncertainty.
suggested_fix: Replace with 'cannot proceed without a decision the user must make (e.g., choosing between two implementation approaches)'.

description: 'Trivial tasks' is vague; only one example given ('reading files'), leaving the boundary ambiguous.
suggested_fix: Replace with 'read-only tasks (file reads, searches, status checks)'.

description: 'significant task' has no size or scope criterion; any task could be argued significant by the model.
suggested_fix: Replace with a concrete threshold, e.g. 'a task that took more than one tool call to complete'.

description: 'complex decisions' is undefined; no criteria for what makes a decision complex enough to warrant a phone call.
suggested_fix: Replace with 'decisions requiring trade-off evaluation between two or more non-equivalent approaches'.

description: 'prestart' script runs 'bun install --silent' on every server start, fetching remote packages from the registry each invocation; combined with semver ranges, the installed dependency set can change between starts.
suggested_fix: Remove the 'prestart' script and document a one-time 'bun install' setup step in the README.

description: @ngrok/ngrok opens an outbound public internet tunnel on every server start; intentional for Twilio webhook delivery but means every run exposes a new public endpoint.
suggested_fix: Document the tunnel exposure in the README security section; consider restricting ngrok tunnel to Twilio IP ranges if the ngrok SDK supports it.

description: 'bun-types' is pinned to 'latest' with no semver range; resolves to whatever version is current at install time.
suggested_fix: Replace 'latest' with a concrete semver range such as '^1.1.38'.

description: Four runtime dependencies (@modelcontextprotocol/sdk, @ngrok/ngrok, openai, ws) use '^' ranges; minor/patch upgrades are pulled automatically on each bun install.
suggested_fix: Pin runtime dependencies to exact versions to ensure reproducible server behavior.

description: Bash(ls *) declared in allowed-tools but no ls invocation appears in any documented step.
suggested_fix: Remove Bash(ls *) from allowed-tools in the frontmatter.

description: 'gracefully' is a vague quantifier in 'handle ENOENT gracefully'; the expected fallback (return default Access object) should be stated explicitly.
suggested_fix: Replace 'gracefully' with the concrete behavior: 'If file missing, return {dmPolicy:"pairing", allowFrom:[], pending:{}}'.

description: Bash(mkdir *) declared in allowed-tools but no mkdir invocation appears in any configure step; directory creation is delegated to bun scripts.
suggested_fix: Remove Bash(mkdir *) from allowed-tools in the frontmatter.

description: 'complete picture' is a vague quantifier in 'give the user a complete picture'; the numbered list below already specifies the content concretely.
suggested_fix: Drop the 'complete picture' phrase; the numbered list (Credentials, Access, What next) is the spec.

description: plugin.json declares version 0.4.0 but package.json and server.ts MCP registration both declare 0.1.0; tooling that correlates these will see inconsistent versions.
suggested_fix: Align all three version strings to a single value, preferably driven from package.json.

description: start script runs 'bun install' on every MCP server launch, resolving and downloading dependencies at runtime rather than at install time, creating a supply-chain window.
suggested_fix: Move dependency installation to a postinstall hook or require users to run 'bun install' once; use 'bun run --frozen-lockfile' in start to prevent silent upgrades.

description: Auto-installs qrcode-terminal via Bun.spawnSync if node_modules is missing; same supply-chain risk as the package.json start script finding.
suggested_fix: Remove the auto-install block; print a clear error directing the user to run 'bun install' in the plugin directory instead.

description: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk uses '^1.0.0' and qrcode-terminal uses '^0.12.0'; caret ranges allow unreviewed minor/patch version bumps on each install.
suggested_fix: Pin to exact versions or commit a bun.lockb and use '--frozen-lockfile' in all install invocations.

description: '--shell=bun' arg routes npm script execution through Bun's built-in shell rather than /bin/sh.
fp_reason: '--shell=bun' selects Bun's cross-platform shell, which is more restricted than /bin/sh and does not enable arbitrary shell injection; this is a safer choice, not a risk.
rule_gap: Rule should distinguish between OS shell (sh/bash) and sandboxed runtime shells (bun shell, deno shell) which have narrower attack surfaces.

description: plugin.json (0.4.0) and package.json/server.ts (0.1.0) track versions independently; the public plugin version has diverged from the npm package version.
suggested_fix: Use a single source-of-truth version field, e.g. read it from package.json at build time or keep both files in sync via a release script.

description: Agent defines no example blocks; zero examples leave the model without calibration anchors for correct vs. incorrect behavior.
suggested_fix: Add at least two ## Example sections with concrete before/after prompt-response pairs.

description: No output format section; agent provides no guidance on expected response structure, length constraints, or rendering conventions.
suggested_fix: Add an ## Output Format section specifying response style, length, and any mandatory structural elements.

description: Vague quantifier: 'genuinely unclear' — does not define a measurable threshold for when to enter plan mode.
suggested_fix: Replace with a concrete condition, e.g., 'more than two mutually exclusive implementation paths exist'.

description: Vague quantifier: 'genuinely independent' — leaves model to judge parallelism threshold without a defined criterion.
suggested_fix: Specify a concrete criterion such as 'no shared output files and no sequential dependency between agents'.

description: Vague quantifier: '尽量' (try to / as much as possible) appears 5 times (lines 27, 29, 31, 32, 46); each instance avoids a concrete trigger or threshold.
suggested_fix: Replace each '尽量' with a specific condition or threshold that makes the guidance actionable and deterministic.

description: spawn() called with shell:true; command string is derived from process.argv.slice(2) or HELLO2CC_CCSTATUSLINE_COMMAND env var, creating a shell injection surface if either source is attacker-controlled.
fp_reason: shell:true is intentional design for a bridge script that must execute a user-configured downstream command; the script is not invoked by any hook in hooks.json and the command source is the developer, not untrusted hook input flowing from Claude's tool pipeline.
rule_gap: SEC-shell-true should distinguish between hook-invoked scripts processing user input and standalone dev-utility bridge scripts where shell:true is an expected implementation choice.
suggested_fix: If hardening is desired, accept the downstream command as a validated array of argv tokens and use spawn(cmd, args, {shell:false}) instead.

description: fetch() to api.github.com at runtime; GH_TOKEN / GITHUB_TOKEN env vars are read and sent as an Authorization Bearer header. Dev-only utility; not reachable from any hook invocation.
suggested_fix: Document the network dependency and token usage in README; add a --no-network fallback that omits acknowledgement resolution when the token is absent.

description: HELLO2CC_DEBUG_ROUTE_PATH env var controls the destination path of writeFileSync without path validation; a maliciously set env var could direct writes outside the repo.
suggested_fix: Validate the resolved path against a known safe root (plugin data dir or os.tmpdir()) before calling writeFileSync.

description: Default downstream command is 'npx -y ccstatusline@latest'; @latest is unpinned and will silently pull future versions on every invocation, introducing supply-chain risk.
suggested_fix: Pin to a specific version tag, e.g., 'npx ccstatusline@1.2.3', and update explicitly on each plugin release.

description: Empty $ARGUMENTS not validated: running /review-loop with no argument silently creates a state file with a blank task body and starts the loop. The standalone setup-review-loop.sh correctly exits with an error for empty input but the command's inline bash omits this check.
suggested_fix: Add a guard before the state-file write: if [ -z "$ARGUMENTS" ]; then echo 'Error: No task description provided.' && exit 1; fi

description: Multi-step command body (setup → implement → stop → run Codex → address feedback) presented in unnumbered prose paragraphs rather than a numbered list, making sequencing ambiguous.
suggested_fix: Replace the prose flow with numbered steps: 1. Run setup bash. 2. Implement task. 3. When done, stop — hook will block and provide runner script. 4. Execute runner script. 5. Read review and address findings.

description: Command declares argument-hint but the body never specifies behavior when $ARGUMENTS is blank. Duplicate of Bug #1; counted as quality penalty too.
suggested_fix: Add explicit empty-input handling in the body: 'If no task description is provided, report an error and exit without creating state.'

description: No output format defined. The command ends with behavioral RULES but provides no report template or completion summary structure for what Claude should say when the review loop finishes.
suggested_fix: Add a Report section: 'Report: Review loop complete (ID: X). Addressed N findings: [list]. Skipped M findings: [list with reasons].'

description: Vague quantifier: 'thoroughly and completely' has no measurable criteria.
suggested_fix: Replace with specific expectations e.g. 'Implement all acceptance criteria, add tests for each new function, and verify no existing tests break.'

description: Vague quantifier: 'well-structured' has no measurable criteria.
suggested_fix: Specify the structural expectation: e.g. 'following existing module boundaries and naming conventions.'

description: Vague quantifier: 'well-tested' has no measurable criteria.
suggested_fix: Specify: e.g. 'with unit tests for each new function and integration tests for new endpoints.'

description: Multi-step body (check active → read state → remove files → report) presented in unnumbered prose; the four sequential steps have no explicit numbering.
suggested_fix: Number the steps: 1. Check if active. 2. If active, read state. 3. Remove state/lock/generated files. 4. Report cancellation with phase and review ID.

description: REVIEW_LOOP_CODEX_FLAGS is read from the environment and expanded unquoted at line 350 into a heredoc-generated shell script. If the variable contains shell metacharacters (;, &&, |), they are baked into .claude/review-loop-run-codex.sh and execute when Claude runs bash on it.
suggested_fix: Validate REVIEW_LOOP_CODEX_FLAGS against ^[a-zA-Z0-9 _=-]*$ before use, or store flags as an array and pass them safely rather than relying on unquoted word-splitting in a generated script.

description: The UX agent section of build_review_prompt() instructs the Codex agent to run 'npm install -g agent-browser' with no version pin. If the package name is squatted or typosquatted, a Codex agent operating on a UI project will install a malicious package.
suggested_fix: Pin to a specific version (npm install -g agent-browser@<version>) or document agent-browser as a manual prerequisite and remove the auto-install suggestion from the prompt.

description: Script header uses ERR trap for cleanup but omits 'set -u' and 'set -o pipefail'. Unbound variables silently produce empty strings; pipeline failures in the middle of a compound command may go undetected.
suggested_fix: Change shebang line to: set -euo pipefail. The existing ERR trap already handles cleanup so the risk of double-cleanup is low.

description: Install instruction 'npm install -g @openai/codex' has no version pin. A breaking change in the Codex CLI could silently break the review workflow without any error at install time.
suggested_fix: Pin to a minimum known-working version, e.g. 'npm install -g @openai/codex@<version>'.

description: scripts/setup-review-loop.sh is a fully-implemented setup script with proper dependency and empty-input checks, but commands/review-loop.md embeds equivalent logic inline and never calls the script. The script has no documented callers and may drift from the inline bash over time.
suggested_fix: Either delete the script and rely solely on the inline bash, or refactor the command to call the script (which also fixes Bug #1 since the script already validates empty input).

description: "A handful of dimensions" — vague quantifier (comparable to R01 'several') with no measurable criterion for count.
suggested_fix: Replace with a concrete range, e.g. '3–5 dimensions'.

description: "a few lines: parse the threshold flag" — vague quantifier (comparable to R01 'some') with no measurable criterion.
suggested_fix: Replace with a concrete count, e.g. '~5 lines'.

description: "without meaningfully different framings" — 'meaningfully' is a vague modifier with no operationalized criterion for when framing difference is sufficient.
suggested_fix: Define a concrete test, e.g. 'briefs that target different files, hypotheses, or gate names are considered distinct'.

description: "a meaningfully different idea after an evaluated/discarded outcome" — same vague modifier as optimize/SKILL.md L147; subagents cannot determine what 'meaningful' means without a threshold.
suggested_fix: Replace with a concrete decision rule, e.g. 'a different file, function, or approach that was not already attempted on this branch'.

description: subprocess.run calls the claude CLI (network call to Anthropic API) with a prompt constructed from internal CASES data. No shell=True; inputs are not from untrusted external sources. Eval-tooling context only.
suggested_fix: Document that this script makes outbound API calls in the README; guard with a --dry-run flag for CI environments that restrict network access.

description: subprocess.run calls the claude CLI with a hardcoded prompt string for trial execution. No shell=True; no user-controlled input in the command array.
suggested_fix: Same as generate_fixture.py: document network dependency and add --dry-run flag.

description: subprocess.run calls the claude CLI as an LLM judge with a prompt assembled from ground truth + model output JSON. No shell=True; data is local fixture content, not external user input.
suggested_fix: Document network dependency; optionally add a --no-llm flag to skip the judge and use only the strict scorer.

description: Writes raw LLM output to /tmp/rlm_narr_{case_id}_raw.txt on JSON parse failure. case_id is drawn from the hardcoded CASES dict so no traversal risk, but /tmp writes are non-portable on Windows.
suggested_fix: Use tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(prefix='rlm_narr_', suffix='.txt', delete=False) for cross-platform portability.

description: Creates trial directory in tempfile.gettempdir() for test isolation. uuid4 suffix prevents collisions; intentional isolation pattern.
fp_reason: tempfile.gettempdir() is the standard cross-platform mechanism for temporary directories; this is intentional test-isolation, not a security risk.
rule_gap: The rule should distinguish between intentional temp-dir isolation patterns and uncontrolled writes to /tmp with user-controlled paths.

description: EVO_TRACES_DIR env var determines where trace files are written; EVO_RESULT_PATH determines the result file path. By design (evo wire protocol); caller is evo run which controls these vars.
fp_reason: EVO_TRACES_DIR and EVO_RESULT_PATH are the documented evo SDK contract; they are always set by the trusted evo CLI, not by untrusted user input.
rule_gap: The rule should account for env vars that are part of a framework's published API contract, not arbitrary external input.
suggested_fix: Add a comment noting that these vars must be set by the evo CLI, not by untrusted input.

description: Runtime deps flask>=3.0.0, portalocker>=2.8.0, pyyaml>=6.0.0 use open >= specifiers. uv.lock pins exact versions for managed installs but pipx/pip users without the lockfile may pull future breaking majors.
suggested_fix: Add upper bounds: flask>=3.0.0,<4; portalocker>=2.8.0,<3; pyyaml>=6.0.0,<7.

description: Description is a one-phrase summary ('Install Wasp agent skills...that add Wasp knowledge...') rather than 3+ specific trigger phrases matching real user queries.
suggested_fix: Rewrite as 3+ trigger phrases: 'Use when adding Wasp plugins, installing agent skills for Claude Code, or setting up Wasp-specific AI tooling in your project.'

description: No scope note linking to the two closely-related sibling skills (getting-started, guided-tour). Without it, Claude cannot distinguish between them when all three are active.
suggested_fix: Add at end: 'Covers Wasp plugin installation only. For first-run setup see [[getting-started]]; for a project walkthrough see [[guided-tour]].'

description: No scope note linking to guided-tour (natural next step) or add-wasp-skills (optional AI-tooling companion). Skill selection is ambiguous when all three siblings are loaded.
suggested_fix: Add at end: 'Covers initial setup only. For a project walkthrough see [[guided-tour]]; to add Wasp AI plugins see [[add-wasp-skills]].'

description: Description has 2 action phrases ('Take a guided tour', 'walks you through project structure, features, and customization checklist') — R04 requires 3+.
suggested_fix: Expand to 3+ phrases: 'Use when exploring Open SaaS project structure, understanding built-in features, or following the customization checklist step by step.'

description: No scope note linking to getting-started (prerequisite) or add-wasp-skills. Users who haven't completed setup may invoke guided-tour prematurely with no redirect guidance.
suggested_fix: Add at end: 'Prerequisite: complete [[getting-started]] first. To add Wasp AI plugins after the tour, see [[add-wasp-skills]].'

description: Script element created at runtime loading from https://static.reo.dev/<clientID>/reo.js — supply-chain risk if reo.dev CDN is compromised.
suggested_fix: Pin to a specific versioned CDN URL and add a Subresource Integrity (SRI) hash attribute to the script element.

description: PostHog project key CdDd2A0jKTI2vFAsrI9JWm3MqpOcgHz1bMyogAcwsE4 hardcoded in client-side script.
fp_reason: PostHog client project keys are intentionally public and must be embedded in browser code per PostHog's architecture; this is not a secret key.
rule_gap: Rule should distinguish between public client-side analytics keys (PostHog, Segment write keys) and server-side secret keys to avoid false positives on standard analytics integrations.

description: Multiple devDependencies use ^ semver ranges (e.g. eslint ^9.39.4, prettier-plugin-tailwindcss ^0.6.14), allowing minor/patch drift on each install.
suggested_fix: Pin exact versions in package.json and rely on npm ci in CI to ensure reproducible installs.

description: wasp new -t saas base-app downloads a project template from Wasp's servers at script runtime; build reproducibility depends on Wasp CDN availability and template integrity.
suggested_fix: Document the external dependency in a comment; consider caching the base template or verifying a checksum post-download.

suggested_fix: Add a response format note, e.g. 'Present instructions as a numbered list; confirm with the user after each step.'

description: Step 3 uses vague directive 'Walk the user through' without specifying format, depth, or confirmation checkpoints.
suggested_fix: Replace with 'Present each installation step as a numbered list item; pause for user confirmation before proceeding.'

description: Skill declares no output format; no specification of response structure or completion signal.

description: Step 4 uses vague directive 'walk them through the steps' without specifying presentation format or granularity.

description: Skill declares no output format; no specification of section presentation format or tour completion signal.

description: Step 3 item 1 uses unmeasurable qualifiers 'clearly and concisely' with no definition of what constitutes clear or concise output.
suggested_fix: Remove qualifiers or replace with specific constraints, e.g. 'summarize each section in 3-5 bullet points.'

description: 'Keep the pace comfortable' is an unmeasurable directive with no heuristic for determining comfortable pacing.

description: PostHog project API key hardcoded directly in public client-side JS file.
fp_reason: PostHog project API keys are intentionally public — they are used client-side to send analytics events and carry no write or admin privileges.
rule_gap: Rule should exempt client-side analytics keys (PostHog, Segment, Mixpanel) that are public by design from the hardcoded-credentials pattern.
suggested_fix: No change required; key is intentionally public. Optionally inject via build-time env var for configurability.

description: Reo analytics clientID hardcoded in public client-side JS file.
fp_reason: Client-side analytics identifiers (Reo, PostHog, GA) are intentionally embedded in public JS and carry no privileged access.
rule_gap: Rule should exempt analytics client IDs used in public browser scripts from hardcoded-credential findings.
suggested_fix: No change required. Optionally extract to a build-time constant for easier configuration across environments.

description: Production dependencies (stripe, openai, @aws-sdk/*) use caret ^ ranges, allowing automatic minor/patch upgrades that could introduce supply-chain risk.
suggested_fix: Pin exact versions for security-critical packages (stripe, openai, @aws-sdk/*) and rely on a lockfile with CI integrity checks.

description: npm script uses kill -9 with PID derived from grep on ps output; unintended process match could kill a wrong process in a shared environment.

description: Skill instructs Claude to present `curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh` in a Bash code block; Claude Code will execute this directly when the user chooses 'set up now', downloading and running an external shell script without integrity verification.
suggested_fix: Replace with documented out-of-band install step or use checksum-verified download; do not pipe to sh in automated Claude flows.

description: Script is designed to be invoked via `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Q00/ouroboros/main/scripts/install.sh | bash`; any compromise of the GitHub repository or CDN delivers arbitrary code execution to all users who run the install command.
suggested_fix: Publish signed releases with checksums and document verification steps; consider using a package manager exclusively instead of curl-pipe-bash.

description: Script echoes `curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh` as an installation recommendation, instructing users to pipe a second external shell script into sh and compounding supply-chain risk.
suggested_fix: Reference the official uv installation docs URL instead of echoing a curl-pipe-sh command; users should verify instructions from the official source.

description: `urllib.request.urlopen('https://pypi.org/pypi/ouroboros-ai/json', timeout=5)` is called on every session start via session-start.py hook, creating a mandatory external dependency and latency in the hook path.
suggested_fix: Increase cache TTL or make update checks opt-in via a prefs flag; avoid blocking session start on external network calls.

description: Dynamically loads and executes version-check.py on every SessionStart hook, triggering a PyPI network call; exceptions are silently swallowed which masks connectivity or SSL failures.
suggested_fix: Add explicit error logging distinguishing network failures from version parse failures; consider running version check asynchronously.

description: `curl -s --max-time 3 https://api.github.com/repos/Q00/ouroboros/releases/latest` runs on every interview invocation for a version pre-check; not piped to shell but adds external dependency to every interview.
suggested_fix: Move version check to session-start.py where caching is already implemented; remove redundant check from interview skill.

description: `ouroboros-ai[mcp,claude]` has no version constraint in the MCP server command; a future breaking release will silently degrade or break existing installs.
suggested_fix: Pin to a range: `"--from", "ouroboros-ai[mcp,claude]>=0.36.0,<1.0.0"` or use a lock file mechanism.

description: Hook command `python3 "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/session-start.py"` interpolates an environment variable; a CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT value containing spaces or shell metacharacters could alter script resolution or cause command injection.

description: eval "$(jq -r '...export \(.key)=\"\(.value)\"' scripts/ci-secrets.json)" — JSON key names are not shell-escaped. A tampered ci-secrets.json with a key containing shell metacharacters (semicolons, backticks, $()) would execute arbitrary code.
suggested_fix: Use 'export \(.key)=\(.value | @sh)' and validate key names match ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ before eval. Private disclosure required for HIGH severity.

description: eval "$(jq -r '...export \(.key)=\(.value | @sh)' $SECRETS_JSON)" — values are @sh-escaped and keys are filtered to VITE_ prefix, but the eval of jq output and the user-controlled $SECRETS_JSON path still introduce risk in multi-user CI environments.
suggested_fix: Confirm SECRETS_JSON points to the expected path before calling jq; consider replacing eval with explicit variable assignments for the small set of known VITE_ variables.

description: eval "$joined" where values are printf %q-escaped but key names from the .env file are not validated. A .env key containing shell special characters would be injected directly into the eval string.
suggested_fix: Validate each key against ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$ before appending to exports; skip or warn on invalid keys.

description: The $FILTER argument (line 11, caller-supplied jq expression) is passed directly into jq without sanitization. A caller providing a malicious jq filter could exfiltrate data or cause unexpected eval behavior.
suggested_fix: Document clearly that $FILTER is trusted-caller-only input; add a comment warning against passing externally-sourced values as the filter argument.

description: postinstall runs install.js which fetches a platform-specific binary from GitHub Releases over HTTPS and places it in bin/. SHA-256 is verified but the download and installation happen automatically on npm install.
suggested_fix: Add an OPENHUMAN_SKIP_INSTALL=1 environment variable guard in install.js so CI and audit environments can npm install without triggering the binary fetch.

description: postinstall: 'husky' runs git hooks setup automatically on npm install. Husky is a well-known tool with small attack surface, but any postinstall constitutes an automatic execution surface.
suggested_fix: No action required unless restricting all auto-execution at install time. Consider 'prepare' script instead of 'postinstall' for husky to avoid running on --production installs.

description: export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$INSTALL_ROOT/bin:$PATH" prepends using $INSTALL_ROOT which defaults to a caller-controlled path. In shared CI environments, a poisoned INSTALL_ROOT could shadow system binaries.
suggested_fix: Resolve INSTALL_ROOT to a canonical absolute path and reject values containing '..' or paths outside expected directories before using in PATH.
